partner_context.their_ambition: You run Abu Dhabi's public marine network across an island capital — water taxis and ferries linking Yas, Saadiyat, Reem, the Corniche and Al Raha — and you keep opening new terminals to grow it.
partner_context.their_pressure: Growth across a low-lying island city and UAE Net Zero 2050 both demand a clean, low-wake fleet that can thread the mangrove channels and dredged lagoons between the islands.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined upgrade to the network you already run — faster and quieter island connections, additive to your existing water-taxi and ferry services.

hero.title: Abu Dhabi ITC × Navier — a zero-emission foiling tier across the island capital
hero.subtitle: A faster, quieter layer on the water taxis and ferries you already run — connecting Yas, Saadiyat, Reem, the Corniche and Al Raha, and decarbonizing the network under UAE Net Zero 2050.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a software-defined, zero-emission foiling tier to Abu Dhabi's public marine network — quiet and low-wake through the mangrove channels and dredged lagoons. It speeds the island connections you already run, widens access, and gives ITC a credible decarbonization path under UAE Net Zero 2050.

why_now: Abu Dhabi already runs public water taxis and ferries across its islands — over 700,000 passengers since launch — and keeps opening terminals (Saadiyat Marina & Ferry Terminal, Rabdan Marina). UAE Net Zero 2050 mandates a clean fleet. Foiling is the natural upgrade: faster, near-silent, low-wake through the channels, and far more efficient per passenger-mile. A demo vessel is in the UAE now.

proof_points.claim: Abu Dhabi already runs public water transport.
proof_points.evidence: ITC and Abu Dhabi Maritime have carried over 700,000 water-taxi and ferry passengers since launch, with new terminals at Saadiyat and Rabdan.
An updated public water-transport schedule and new stations (incl. Yas Bay) went live in October 2025.
UAE Net Zero 2050 and the Abu Dhabi Environment Vision require a clean fleet across all modes.

proof_points.claim: The fleet model is real and at scale.
proof_points.evidence: ~100 vessels / $100M / 3-year phasing proving the network model in the Maldives.

objections.concern: Will foiling work in the shallow mangrove channels?
objections.response: Yes — vessels run conventionally and low-wake through the channels and lagoons, and only foil on the open stretches where cleared. Low wake actually protects the mangroves.
Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the long-range hybrid covers the Abu Dhabi–Dubai leg with no offshore charging at all.

objections.concern: Is foiling safe across the island channels?
objections.response: Foiling is software-governed — geofenced no-foil zones at berths and bridges, automatic speed and wake limits, and conventional low-speed handling in shared water.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, the Maldives-proven network playbook, certification and operations.
the_ask.partner_brings: Network integration with Abu Dhabi Maritime, berth access, and regulatory cover.
the_ask.next_step: A Yas–Saadiyat–Corniche pilot, co-specified with ITC.

close.title: A clean foiling tier across the island capital.
close.body: Start on Yas, Saadiyat and the Corniche, scale across the full island network, then add the domestic UAE express — a zero-emission upgrade to the marine network Abu Dhabi already runs, advancing Net Zero 2050.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.
